Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - postcall recap

Thanks for the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we agreed: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Validate p95 / p99 end-to-end latency targets for your primary inference path (user client -> model response delivered).
- Current provider observed (your notes): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s for typical 512-token responses under steady load; spikes during peak concurrency.
- Finlytics goals: p95 <=250ms, p99 <=600ms for interactive flows (streaming enabled). Throughput target ~500 requests/sec with typical concurrency ~80-120 active streams.
- Streaming: incremental tokens via SSE/Chunked responses are required for product UX. You measure latency as time to first token and time to final token; both matter.

Next steps (action items):
1) You -> share traffic shape and a sample of latency logs (you mentioned a CSV) so we can baseline.
2) Redwood -> provide a proposed test plan and initial target configurations (model variant, instance types, concurrency/throughput profiles).
3) Pilot kickoff: propose a 2-week pilot where we run side-by-side tests against your current provider + Redwood hosted API (same model/seed prompts).

We attached an internal test-plan stub on our side and will follow up with a more detailed plan (Marissa will lead the technical testing). Please confirm Sam (and copy your eng alias) that the CSV you mentioned is the right sample.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - postcall recap

Thanks Laura — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side before we move to the test plan:

- The numbers we shared (p95 ~420ms / p99 ~1.2s) are end-to-end measured from our client (browser) to last-token-received, including our network. We can strip client-side rendering time if helpful, but the UX team measures from request send -> final token delivered.
- Streaming: yes, we need streaming first-token latency to be low (goal: first token <120ms ideally) and final token p95/p99 within the numbers above.
- Warm starts: we see significant variation on cold cold-starts for new containers; our SLA expectation is for steady-state. Please confirm how you measure cold vs warm start in the test plan.

I've attached a sample export of recent latency points (finlytics_latency_samples.csv). It includes 10k rows across peak and off-peak windows. Also looping in our eng lead (eng@finlytics.com) for scheduling.

We'll review Redwood's test plan once you share.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider) - test plan and measurement details

Hi Sam / team — thanks for the sample CSV and the clear goals. Attaching a concise test plan and a measurement script to start (see attachments). High-level notes here so everyone has context: 

Measurement definitions (what we'll report):
- p95 / p99 end-to-end: measured as time from client request HEADERS_SENT to last byte of final token received (includes network + server processing). We'll provide separate columns for time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token.
- Steady-state vs cold-start: steady-state is defined as after a 3-minute warmup with target concurrency; cold-start measured from an idle endpoint after full scale-down. We'll capture both.
- Streaming metrics: report time-to-first-token p50/p95/p99 and token-delivery throughput (tokens/sec) for streaming sessions.

Recommended baseline test configuration (hosted API target):
- Model: open-llama-*-512 variant (match your current model size used in CSV), with quantized runtime.
- Instance profile: single-tenant GPU instance (A100 class) for pilot; we'll also record multi-tenant SLOs on our shared pool to show economics differences.
- Traffic shape: mimic your CSV distribution (we will ingest your sample). Target throughput: 500 req/sec sustained with 80-120 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Latency targets we will validate against: p95 <=250ms (time-to-last-token) and p99 <=600ms for the steady-state. First-token target: p95 <=120ms.

Testing notes and caveats:
- Batching and KV cache effects: continuous batching improves unit cost but can increase tail latency. For interactive flows we will cap batching window and prioritize low-latency execution.
- Network locality: we'll run tests from your region (us-west) to eliminate cross-region noise.
- Model warm-up script: included in latency_test_script.sh — please let us know if you want us to run this from your infra or ours.

Attachments (stubs): redwood_test_plan_v1.pdf, latency_test_script.sh.

Proposed next steps:
1) Finlytics: confirm the model variant you want us to test and confirm the CSV sample is representative.
2) Redwood: we will provision test endpoints and share a JMeter/harness config; run side-by-side tests next week (Mon/Tue preferred).
3) Sync call after pilot to review p95/p99 curves and discuss rollout options (dedicated vs hosted routing policy).

If everything looks good I'll schedule the test runs and send invites.

Thanks,
Marissa
